payload.title: propose_self_change appends the open self_change proposal (uuid id) before it records the HUMAN_REQUIRED adjudication in a separate write, so a failure of the second write leaves an orphan open proposal, a mission that is not parked and a fresh proposal on the next request (latent: needs a lock or IO fault between the two writes)
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/self_improvement.py:1124-1130 (record_proposal runs first, record_human_required second, no shared transaction)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/proposal.py:68-70 (every call mints a new proposal-<uuid4> id, so a retry cannot reuse the orphan)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/self_improvement.py:298-306 (open_self_change_adjudication reads only HUMAN_REQUIRED records, so an orphan proposal is invisible to the duplicate guard)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/self_change_bridge.py:168-193 (the mission is parked only after propose_self_change returns)
payload.rule_violated: Two writes that must stand or fall together need one transaction (the ledger's own state_transaction discipline in human_required._write_human_required_record).
payload.notes: If record_human_required raises after record_proposal succeeded (a state lock timeout, an IO error), the exception leaves an open self_change row in proposals.jsonl, no adjudication and a mission still waiting for its self-change answer. The next cycle mints another request and another proposal-<uuid>; the duplicate guard looks only at HUMAN_REQUIRED records, so open proposals accumulate with no question to a person. Narrow: the profile gates of both surfaces refuse together under frozen and observe, so only a lock or IO fault splits them. Close condition: propose_self_change writes the adjudication first or both writes share one state_transaction; a test makes record_human_required raise and asserts proposals.jsonl gains no open self_change row and a retry yields exactly one proposal (red today).
